approved: Higher Education Support Amendment (Further Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2013
Tertiary Education, Skills, Science and Research

Supported the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill improving VET FEE-HELP administration, said only 112 of about 2,000 eligible providers currently offer VET FEE-HELP, and said a quarter of 20 to 24 year olds were not in full time education or work in 2012.

Supported the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill, contrasted nearly $49 million in federal funding for the University of Southern Queensland with Queensland government TAFE cuts, and said a state jobs training program scrapped by the LNP had helped 57,000 Queenslanders into work for a $90 million investment.

Supported the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill, said only 112 of about 2,000 eligible training providers offer VET FEE-HELP with just 39,124 students accessing it in 2011, and welcomed federal funding for Charles Sturt University's Wagga Wagga life sciences hub.

Closed debate on the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill, said the current HELP repayment threshold is $49,096, and said the changes followed the April 2012 COAG National Partnership Agreement and a September 2011 review of VET FEE-HELP.

Three bills—the Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment Bill 2013, the Higher Education Support Amendment (Further Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2013, and the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill 2013—were introduced together, with a motion to proceed without formalities and be read a first time agreed to.

The coalition supported the bill, which introduced recommendations from a 2011 review of VET FEE-HELP to reduce administrative complexity and increase provider numbers. The Greens supported the bill but opposed shifting VET costs to students via income-contingent loans and the commercialisation of the VET sector.
